capabilities: scan a service root directory for manifest.json files
run configured local executable, Python, and batch commands
read service status.json files and recent command output
display Windows Task Scheduler status and warning or error events
create and edit service manifests from Obsidian
extras: Windows-only; reads and writes files outside the vault and executes local commands, which the README flags as a prototype-stage security caution.
problem: Obsidian has no way to discover, launch, and observe status of local services and scheduled tasks from within the app.
summary: Windows-only plugin that discovers, runs, and monitors local services and tools from a workspace inside Obsidian.
